# Alynne Davis, MA, LCMHC

> Eating disorder, body image and trauma therapy for women in Charlotte, North Carolina, and online across North Carolina and South Carolina. For women who take care of everyone else.

Alynne Davis is a Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor and expressive arts therapist in Charlotte, NC. She has practised for over a decade and did her graduate work on how expressive arts therapy informs the treatment of eating disorders.

Her clients are typically high-functioning women who look fine from the outside. They hold their families, their work and often a parent together, and the cost shows up in their relationship with food and their bodies. Many have never said any of it out loud before the first session.

## What makes her approach different

- The work treats eating disorders and body image through the lens of self-abandonment, the habit of monitoring and managing yourself until your own needs disappear. Food is usually where that cost becomes visible.
- She does not ask clients to diet, count calories or track weight. Weight is not treated as a measure of health, worth or progress.
- The eating disorder work is structured and moves through phases, and trauma work is woven through it rather than saved until afterwards.
- The work happens in the body as well as in conversation, using somatic and nervous system practices, parts work, and creative and expressive arts. Clients do not need to be artistic.
- Treatment is typically 20 to 40 weeks. Recovery is treated as realistic, not aspirational.

## Credentials and scope

- MA, Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor (LCMHC)
- Expressive arts therapist, over a decade in practice
- Licensed to provide therapy in North Carolina and South Carolina only
- Certified in nutrition. Not a dietitian or physician. Does not prescribe medication, supplements or meal plans
- Primarily a private-pay practice. Superbills are provided for out-of-network reimbursement, and Mentaya can be used to check benefits and file claims
- A limited number of sliding scale places are available by application

## Specialties

- Eating disorders: binge eating, anorexia, bulimia, orthorexia, emotional eating, chronic dieting, and the binge and restrict cycle
- Body image and body shame
- Trauma and complex PTSD, including emotionally immature or unavailable parents
- ADHD in women, including late diagnosis, masking and burnout, and its overlap with eating behaviour
- Anxiety, including high-functioning anxiety
- Perinatal and postpartum mental health
- Athletes and former athletes, including the loss of identity and body trust after leaving a sport
- Adolescents and their families, using family-based therapy
- Life transitions: divorce, motherhood, midlife, perimenopause, identity loss

## Common questions she answers

- Do I need a diagnosis to get help? No. Most women who come to her have never been diagnosed and many have never spoken about it before.
- Is it bad enough to get help? That question is itself one of the most common reasons women wait years longer than they needed to.
- Do I have to talk about weight? No. Weighing is optional, discussed in advance, and never used as a measure of progress.
- Do I need to be artistic to do expressive arts therapy? No. Creative expression here means finding a way to reach what words alone cannot.
- Is coaching the same as therapy? No. Coaching is forward-focused and is not therapy, not covered by insurance, and not a substitute for clinical care.

## Ways to work with her

- [Therapy](https://alynnedavis.com/services/): ongoing weekly work, in person in Charlotte or online across NC and SC. The main way she works.
- [Intensives](https://alynnedavis.com/intensives/): focused extended sessions, a few hours to a few days, for going deeper faster or for building momentum before weekly work begins.
- [Coaching](https://alynnedavis.com/embodied-reclamation-studio/): forward-focused work through Embodied Reclamation Studio, for women outside North Carolina and South Carolina. Not therapy.

## Free resources

- [Ten Minutes That Are Only Yours](https://alynnedavis.com/ten-minutes/): a free guided audio practice for the woman who takes care of everyone
- [Beyond the Scale](https://alynnedavis.com/free-guide/): a free guide on food, weight and recovery
- [Eating disorder glossary](https://alynnedavis.com/eating-disorder-glossary/): plain-language definitions of eating disorder terms

## Areas served

Charlotte, Ballantyne, South Charlotte, Matthews, Pineville, Huntersville, Cornelius, Davidson, Mooresville, Waxhaw, and Concord in North Carolina. Fort Mill, Rock Hill, Tega Cay, and Indian Land in South Carolina. Telehealth throughout both states, including Raleigh, Asheville, Durham, Wilmington, Columbia SC, and Greenville SC.
